gap: An existing import job can commit after source deletion reads facts but before deletion marks the job revoked, leaving a newly committed fact ACTIVE.
fix: Lock all existing source jobs in ascending import_job_id before reading facts; preserve job-to-traveler order. Provider disconnect does not prelock one imported job when deleting. Source reconnect/disconnect uses the same stable order.

before.note: One regression proves deleted_facts=0 after injected commit; lock intention/order assertions also fail. Final test assertions corrected plural table names to actual singular schema names.

limitations: SQL FOR UPDATE intent compiled for PostgreSQL; execution and controlled interleaving use isolated SQLite, not PostgreSQL runtime evidence.

Only existing import jobs are serialized. Concurrent creation of a new job with the same source fingerprint remains a phantom-insertion scope needing separate source-level locking design and PostgreSQL proof.
Combined source requires C14 and independent C13 re-review; no upload, merge, deployment or live mutation.
next_task: C14 review this exact existing-job revocation boundary; PostgreSQL contention proof remains HOLD.
